title: Per-language publish adapters and reproducible build recipes with canary publish flow
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Implement per-language publishing adapters (Python, TypeScript, Go) with deterministic build recipes, integrated artifact signing and provenance metadata, and a staged canary publish flow that minimizes blast radius. This ticket covers CI pipeline changes, publish adapters, signer key handling, example publish configs for PyPI/npm/gomod, and developer ergonomics for local dry-run and rollback. Out of scope: changing package names or versioning scheme for existing packages; heavy refactor of current SDK codepaths (small adaptors only).
acceptance_criteria: CI has per-language publish adapters that can build and publish artifacts to test registries with a single step
Artifacts include an attached provenance.json and GPG/ecdsa signature stored alongside the package (or as registry-attested metadata where supported)
Canary publish flow: 3-phase publish to test-registry -> canary channel -> stable channel with automatic health gates in CI
All builds are reproducible given the same input (lockfiles, toolchain versions) and the CI pipeline emits deterministic build metadata
Developer CLI supports dry-run and local signature verification steps
Documentation updated with per-language instructions and rollbacks
Rollbacks can be triggered from CI with a documented procedure and automation for revoking a canary release
technical_notes: Use action matrix to build per-language artifacts in parallel (python wheel/sdist, npm tgz, go module zip)
Create a small adapter layer: scripts/publish_adapters/{python,js,go}.sh that normalize inputs and call shared 'publish-orchestrator' step
Provenance: follow in-toto inspired minimal schema: builder id, command, inputs (lockfile SHAs), output artifact SHA, timestamp
Signing: use ephemeral CI signing key with attestations stored in an internal secure blobstore and registry metadata where possible; long-term HSM/KMS integration planned in follow-up
Canary gating: integrate Console health checks endpoint and synthetic test harness; require < 0.5% failure rate and token cost regression < 5% during canary window
Reproducibility: pin build containers with digest references; record toolchain versions in provenance.json
Rollback: publish a 'yank' artifact or tag depending on registry capabilities; maintain mapping between package version and registry artifact ID in release metadata
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Implement adapters and dry-run publish to internal test registries (1 week). Phase 2: Wire in signature/provenance generation and verification (3 days). Phase 3: Run canary publish for a non-critical SDK patch (monitor 48h). Phase 4: Promote to stable and add docs & automation for rollback. Stop-the-line health gate if any verification or signing step fails.
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter normalization logic
Integration tests: CI pipeline publishes to ephemeral registries and verifies provenance+signature
End-to-end: dry-run local publish reproduces same provenance.json as CI build given same inputs
Canary monitoring: synthetic CI jobs exercising sample SDK flows and measuring latency/cost regression
Security review: verify signing keys lifecycle and least-privilege access to copy artifacts to registries
